Goldens pin an amen-style pattern to exact note count/velocities/pitches; --selftest covers happy path + undo; agent catalog entry + commands.contract test; gate green.

title: Fix the nested-message-loop re-entrancy that crashes headless --selftest
acceptance: The chosen approach removes the nested pump from inside open transactions (or makes re-entrancy provably safe). Verified with the documented Release+ASan 5-way concurrent reproduction: >=20 consecutive runs with zero ASan reports and zero non-zero exits, plus --selftest x3 deterministic and main's native gate green across 3 consecutive runs.
notes: REPRODUCED AND DIAGNOSED 2026-07-18 — full record in docs/worklog/2026-07-18-selftest-sigsegv-reproduction-and-diagnosis.md. Needs Release AND concurrency: Release+ASan 5-way concurrent crashes 2 of 5; Debug+ASan is clean serial and concurrent; the Jul-16 Release binary is clean 6/6 (brackets the regression to after 2026-07-16). ASan names it: heap-buffer-overflow READ in tracktion::engine::AudioFileManager::handleAsyncUpdate(), reached via juce::MessageManager::runDispatchLoopUntil <- MoshOps::importWaveFileToTrack <- cmdImportClip <- cmdAddTestTone. ROOT CAUSE: MoshOps pumps a NESTED MESSAGE LOOP while its own undo transaction is open, which runs queued async work re-entrantly in the middle of a half-finished Tracktion mutation. 12 runDispatchLoopUntil sites in MoshOps.cpp, 4 more in MoshEngine.cpp — a pattern, not a one-off. SCOPE (CORRECTED — an earlier pass wrongly called this headless-only): the pump on the REPRODUCING path (importWaveFileToTrack) is hasAudio-guarded, but 6 of the 15 pumps are NOT guarded and are user-reachable — cmdStopRecording (MoshOps.cpp:5131, pumps x4 right after a real take lands), audio-device setup (MoshOps.cpp:10161), and MoshEngine.cpp:158 / :602 (new + load project), :218 (MIDI enable before restartPlayback), :334 (audio output open). So the re-entrancy hazard IS in the shipped GUI app; what is missing is a reproduction on those paths — a gap in evidence, not evidence of safety. NO FIX SHIPPED: the change touches the single mutation path at 12 sites and needs a design decision (defer the drain past endTxn / settle itemIDs without pumping / make re-entrancy safe), not a guess.

Owner confirmed 2026-07-18 that no build with brain.env has left his machines, so this is latent, not a live leak - no key rotation needed, but it must not ship. Real fix is #403 (server-side proxy), gated on owner task O4.

title: Allowlist the companion server's /command endpoint
acceptance: An explicit COMPANION_COMMANDS allowlist rejects anything outside it with 403 before reaching commandHandler. Catch2 test asserts a known-destructive command (e.g. remove_track) is refused over /command.
notes: RemoteCompanionServer.cpp:279-284 passes the request straight to commandHandler - the same seam WebBridge wires to MoshOps, i.e. the full 200+ command surface, with no allowlist, no screening, no destructive-rate limit. The listener is NOT loopback-bound (:107 createListener with an empty host = all interfaces; it has to be, for the phone). Only the shared pairing token gates it. The in-process agent path IS allowlisted (ui/src/agent/executor.ts:133 validateCommand) and destructive-capped - so the NETWORK-reachable surface has strictly weaker authorization than the local one. Derive the allowlist from what ios/MoshCompanion actually sends.

title: Generate the companion pairing token with a CSPRNG + throttle failed auth
acceptance: makeToken() uses SecRandomCopyBytes (macOS) / BCryptGenRandom (Windows), hex-encoding 32 bytes. authorize() uses a constant-time compare. A per-source failed-attempt counter hard-stops pairing after ~10 misses.
notes: RemoteCompanionProtocol.cpp:62-64 uses juce::Random::getSystemRandom() - a 64-bit LCG, not a CSPRNG; two consecutive nextInt64() draws are deterministically related, so the token carries far less entropy than its length suggests. It is the SOLE auth for a LAN-bound server (see AUD-003). No failed-attempt counter or backoff anywhere in the file. The compare at :50 is a non-constant-time juce::String ==. Partial mitigation verified: a hard 5-minute TTL (RemoteCompanionProtocol.h:28), set once and never refreshed, so the window is genuinely bounded.

title: Implement paste_clip in bridge.mock.ts and cover copy/paste for real
acceptance: `case "paste_clip"` mirrors cmdPasteClip (MoshOps.cpp:4789). A vitest does copySelection -> pasteClipboard -> asserts a second clip exists on the target track, and an e2e covers the Cmd-C/Cmd-V round trip.
notes: store.ts:679 pasteClipboard issues exec('paste_clip'). MoshOps.cpp:1147 dispatches it. bridge.mock.ts has NO case for it and it is not in DEFAULT_OK, so it hits the fail-closed default (:2189) and returns err('unhandled command in dev-mock: paste_clip') - Cmd-V is BROKEN in dev and e2e today. The only test touching the path (menuActions.test.ts:16) replaces pasteClipboard with vi.fn(async()=>{}), so it asserts the menu calls a stub and never that paste works. Copy/paste has zero real coverage.

title: Add a mock-vs-native parity gate for bridge.mock.ts
acceptance: A new contract test parses MoshOps.cpp's dispatch table + handler arg reads and the mock's case blocks, then asserts (a) every native command is handled or on a documented allowlist, and (b) every arg a native handler reads is read by the mock case or listed in a WONTMODEL set with a reason.
notes: bridge.mock.ts is the ONLY backend for all vitest + 23 e2e specs, yet nothing asserts it matches the native surface - while the AGENT catalog has exactly this guard (commands.contract.test.ts:38 parseDispatch). 17 agent-declared args are silently ignored by the mock. Behavioural ones: quantize_notes ignores `strength` entirely and always hard-quantizes (native computes start+(q-start)*strength and clamps division to 0.03125); the load_plugin/load_builtin/load_master_* family ignores `index` and always appends (native inserts at index and returns it); assign_sample ignores gainDb+mode; create_render_layer ignores regionStart/End; export_stems ignores bitDepth/sampleRate. NOTE: no test currently LIES because none exercises these args - this is a coverage gap, not a live false-green. Also fix the two with real product behaviour behind them (quantize strength, plugin index).

title: Stop render_layer / render_ahead_arm blocking the message thread on service spawn
acceptance: No UI-reachable command spawns the generative service synchronously on the message thread. Proven by timing the command with the service down.
notes: execute_command is synchronous on the message thread (unlike brain_chat, which is deliberately Thread::launch'd), so any command that calls ensureServiceRunning() freezes the UI for the full spawn+warmup. This is the documented class that produced a ~1.3-2s freeze on EVERY launch when loadCapabilities() was added to init() (fixed in the playtest-prep push by making the fetch lazy). render_layer / render_ahead_arm are the primary generative actions and still take that path. #349's early-bail only helps the dead-service case.

title: Close two false-green holes in the verification harnesses
acceptance: verify.py --gate cannot pass against a WAV left by a previous run (render output is removed or uniquely named per run, RED-proved). The gate's e2e lane binds to the isolated config/port rather than reusing whatever owns :5173.
notes: Both are vacuous-verification risks of the class this repo has been bitten by three times. (1) verify.py --gate's golden-audio check can pass against a stale WAV from a previous run - a render that silently produces nothing still matches the golden. (2) The gate's e2e lane reuses whatever dev server owns :5173, so a FOREIGN worktree's bundle can silently green the suite (the documented isolated-config gotcha, but the gate itself does not enforce it).

title: Make the gate's Python lane actually run every service test
acceptance: service/stitch_test.py (and any other top-level service test) is executed by the gate. A deliberately broken assertion in it reds the gate.
notes: The gate's pathspec requires a SUBDIRECTORY, so service/stitch_test.py at the top level has never been executed by any gate. Related and separate: the cheap gate's Python suite is path-scoped to touched paths, so a broken service/ test stays invisible until some PR happens to touch service/ - A/B against main before blaming the PR that surfaces it. Also: gate.sh reports SKIPPED python tests as passes, which makes the DoRA merge-math guard a guaranteed no-op in CI.

title: Return an HTTP response when a service route raises
acceptance: do_GET/do_POST wrap dispatch in a top-level handler that returns 500 with a JSON body on an unhandled exception. Test asserts a route that raises still produces a response.
notes: An unhandled route exception currently returns NO HTTP response at all - the native side sees a dropped connection rather than an error, which is much harder to diagnose and can hang a caller that is waiting on a body.

title: Make the Info.plist TCC key injection cover worktree and work-dir builds

notes: Three __TCC_CRASHING_DUE_TO_PRIVACY_VIOLATION__ aborts on 2026-07-18 across TWO bundle locations (~/Mosh/... and ~/Library/Mosh/work/...), plus earlier ones on 07-11 and 07-16. CLAUDE.md records this class as FIXED on 2026-06-27 via the fail-closed cmake/InjectInfoPlistKeys.cmake + the always-run MoshFixInfoPlist target - the fix is real but is evidently not covering the worktree/work-dir build paths. macOS hard-kills the process (SIGABRT), so this is a crash, not a degradation.

title: Give MoshOps a lifetime guard for detached threads and queued callAsync
acceptance: Every detached thread body and every queued callAsync that touches `this` checks a liveness token first. RED-proved by a test that tears the engine down with work in flight.
notes: 12 detached std::thread([this, ...]) in MoshOps.cpp and 14 .detach() sites in src/, with ZERO lifetime-guard mechanism in MoshOps.h (no weak_ptr / SafePointer / WeakReference / alive flag). The `epoch` captures used at MoshOps.cpp:1822, :7637, :8143 are STALENESS guards - they drop superseded results - and do not help here, because reading the epoch already dereferences `this`. Worst instance is cmdMpFetchMissingStems (MoshOps.cpp:3656-3691): a detached thread doing blocking HTTP for seconds, an unsynchronised mpSession_ read, and an unguarded callAsync([this, results]) - and that exact lambda is named in 8 crash dumps. Related to AUD-001 but independently worth fixing.

title: Investigate selftest undo assertions that fail under concurrent load
acceptance: Either the undo behaviour is made load-independent, or the selftest assertion is corrected to match real semantics and the reason is documented. 5-way concurrent runs are clean.
notes: FOUND BY THE AUDIT PASS, new. Running 5 concurrent --selftest processes (isolated session dirs, so NOT the SLF-CONC-001 shared-dir bug) makes 'undo removed the track' fail in ~2 of 5 runs on a current-main Debug+ASan build. IMPORTANT CONTROL: the Jul-16 deployed Release binary fails WORSE under the same 5-way concurrency (1,2,3,5,8 failures across the five runs) than current main does (0,0,0,1,1) - so this fragility is PRE-EXISTING and has substantially improved, not a new regression. Likely an undo-transaction coalescing window that widens under load. Distinct from AUD-001: no crash, just a failed assertion.

title: Bound audio-device startup: a blocking CoreAudio open hangs the app forever with no window and no error
acceptance: Audio-device startup is bounded. If the device does not open within a timeout (~5s), the app STILL shows its window, surfaces an actionable error naming the device, and opens (or links to) the device picker so the user can choose another. The engine reaches a usable no-audio state rather than blocking the message thread. Headless modes (--live-audio-smoke, --selftest, --run-script) fail with a clear message and a non-zero exit instead of hanging indefinitely. Verified by forcing the failure (e.g. a device that does not respond) and observing a window + error, not a hang.
notes: FOUND 2026-07-24 by driving the deployed app on this Mac. Mosh launched, showed NO window, sat at 0% CPU and never recovered - reproducible 3/3, still stuck after 63s. Not a crash: a deadlock on the MAIN THREAD inside audio-device open, BEFORE the window is created, so the user sees only a bouncing dock icon with no feedback whatsoever. Stack: MoshApplication::initialise -> MoshEngine::MoshEngine -> tracktion::engine::Engine::initialise -> juce::AudioDeviceManager::initialiseFromXML -> setAudioDeviceSetup -> CoreAudioClasses::AudioIODeviceCombiner::start -> CoreAudioInternal::start -> AudioDeviceCreateIOProcID_mac_imp -> HALC_ProxyIOContext::_TellServerAboutStreamUsage -> HALC_ProxyObject::SetPropertyData -> mach_msg2_trap (blocked in synchronous IPC to coreaudiod). A second sample caught the sibling frame AudioDeviceStart_mac_imp -> HALB_IOThread::StartAndWaitForState -> __psynch_mutexwait. ISOLATION (already done, do not redo): --live-audio-smoke, which is fully headless with no GUI/WebView, hangs at the IDENTICAL frame - so this is device open, not the UI. coreaudiod itself was HEALTHY throughout (afplay completed normally). The C++ was byte-identical to a build that had launched fine 20 minutes earlier, so the trigger is ENVIRONMENTAL, not a code regression. `sudo killall coreaudiod` cleared it and --live-audio-smoke then passed 14/14. CONTEXT: AudioIODeviceCombiner means JUCE is pairing a SEPARATE input and output device. The machine had a Continuity 'iPhone Microphone' and BlackHole 2ch alongside the built-in mic; CoreAudio logged its input-processing/voice-isolation handler for studio.mosh.app, confirming an INPUT is opened at startup. Note MoshEngine.cpp's session/audio-device.xml restore and the MOSH_AUDIO_INPUT_DEVICE / MOSH_AUDIO_OUTPUT_DEVICE env knobs both run AFTER this hang point, so neither is a usable workaround today - the fix has to bound the open inside (or around) Engine::initialise. WHY IT MATTERS: this is a daily-driver blocker. The failure is invisible and unrecoverable without Activity Monitor plus a sudo coreaudiod restart, which no ordinary user will find. A bounded wait plus an honest error turns a dead app into a recoverable one. FIXED 2026-07-25: te::Engine's autoInitialiseDeviceManager is now ALWAYS false; MoshEngine::openAudioDeviceBounded runs a bounded PROBE (platform AudioIODeviceType, open+start+stop+close, on a worker thread, default 5s via MOSH_AUDIO_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS) and only then does the real te::DeviceManager::initialise inline on the message thread. On timeout the probe is abandoned+leaked on purpose (freeing a device stuck in mach_msg would move the hang into the destructor), audioOpen goes false, and the engine lands in the well-trodden headless no-audio state - so the app still comes up and still quits. NOT juce::AudioDeviceManager for the probe: its initialise() also opens MIDI (openLastRequestedMidiDevices -> MidiInput::getAvailableDevices), a process-wide singleton under JUCE_ASSERT_MESSAGE_THREAD - driving it off the message thread is a real race (caught by lldb during this fix). start() is in the probe deliberately: the AUD-017 stack wedged in AudioDeviceCreateIOProcID, reached from start(), not open(). Recovery: retry_audio_device (UI-only, non-undoable, refuses without touching hardware when audioRequested() is false, which is what keeps --selftest hermetic) + an AudioDeviceNotice banner in both shells. MOSH_AUDIO_OPEN_STALL_MS forces the timeout branch on healthy hardware. Cost: one extra HAL open per audio launch, measured at 152ms (3 runs). Verified: forced failure -> honest error naming device AND input, exit 8, no hang; healthy --live-audio-smoke 14/14; --selftest 1797x3; Catch2 2212; vitest 1757; e2e 187; probe-clamp RED-proven (7 failures under sabotage).

title: Launching the built Mosh.app binary directly is killed by TCC at ~3s — GUI verification silently impossible without `open`
acceptance: Either (a) running `build-*/Mosh_artefacts/<cfg>/Mosh.app/Contents/MacOS/Mosh` from a terminal reaches a live window and stays up, or (b) it fails with a message that names TCC and tells the caller to use `open -n <bundle>` instead of dying with a bare SIGABRT. The preferred fix is (a) via lazy speech authorization: nothing may call SFSpeechRecognizer requestAuthorization until the user actually starts voice input, so a launch that never touches voice never asks. Verified by launching the binary path directly (not via `open`) and observing a window, and by confirming hands-free still prompts + works on first use.
notes: FOUND 2026-07-25 while verifying AUD-017. SYMPTOM: `.../Mosh.app/Contents/MacOS/Mosh` from a shell exits 134 (SIGABRT) after ~3s, with the window never appearing. stderr ends innocuously at '[webview] camera permission delegate installed' / the wave-device list, so it reads as a product crash. DIAGNOSIS (do not redo): the .ips says termination namespace TCC, 'attempted to access privacy-sensitive data without a usage description ... NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription', faulting thread inside __TCC_CRASHING_DUE_TO_PRIVACY_VIOLATION__ <- __TCCAccessRequest_block_invoke <- xpc reply. The key IS present in the built bundle (plutil confirms all three: Speech, Microphone, Camera), so the 2026-06-27 missing-plist-key fix is NOT regressed. RULED OUT: (1) plist-not-bound — the Debug bundle is linker-signed adhoc with 'Info.plist=not bound', but a `codesign --force --deep --sign -` that binds it ('Info.plist entries=16') STILL dies at 3s; (2) my AUD-017 device-probe — A/B'd against stashed-clean main in the same build dir, baseline dies identically at 3s. WHAT DOES WORK: `open -n <bundle>` — the SAME bundle stays alive indefinitely. So the discriminator is LaunchServices vs direct exec: for a non-LaunchServices launch macOS attributes the privacy request to the RESPONSIBLE process (the terminal / the agent's shell), which carries no usage description, and hard-kills. It also does not reproduce under lldb, which makes it look flaky. WHY IT MATTERS: this is the default way a developer or an agent verifies a GUI change, and the failure is a bare SIGABRT with no hint — today it cost time twice and was briefly misattributed to a real code change. THE PRODUCT-SIDE FIX WORTH TAKING: authorization is only requested at startup because hands-free listening auto-starts; requesting it lazily on first voice use fixes direct launches AND stops asking for a permission many users never need, which is the progressive-disclosure posture the rest of the UI follows. If lazy auth is rejected, the fallback is a startup guard that detects the responsible-process case and logs the `open -n` instruction instead of aborting, plus a line in docs/VERIFICATION.md.

title: Replace AUD-017's process-local timeout with killable audio-device preflight isolation
acceptance: The exact saved or default JUCE DEVICESETUP is opened only in a killable child before Tracktion touches CoreAudio. Persisted and encoded setup XML rejects DTD/entity declarations before JUCE parsing. On timeout the child is killed and reaped; degraded list_audio_devices and Retry return without re-entering the poisoned HAL; visible Settings remains responsive. Default, output-only, and input-only argument transport, adversarial nested-entity rejection, Linux no-app configuration, native UI, and the full exact-SHA gate all pass.
notes: SUPERSEDES the implementation diagnosis in done record AUD-017 without erasing its historical baseline evidence. Production-v2 issue #527 proved the abandoned in-process worker was not safe: the wedged thread retained process-local CoreAudio/HAL state, and opening Settings synchronously scanned devices into the same poisoned process. PR #528 replaces the worker/leak design with a same-executable child probe carrying the complete saved/default setup, kills and reaps it on timeout, and suppresses hardware enumeration while degraded. A later exact-SHA security review proved that the byte cap alone did not bound JUCE's DTD/entity expansion in the parent; the successor rejects those declarations before both parent and child parse boundaries and carries the small entity payload as a regression. Because a Git commit cannot contain its own final SHA, current acceptance is bound by the external issue #527 manifest: its head/base must match the live PR, every referenced artifact hash must verify, all hosted checks must pass, and all five exact-SHA lanes must pass. Any commit invalidates that manifest. PR #528 remains owner-ordered behind draft PR #523 and must rebase, regate, repeat native UI, and repeat review after that merge. Separate MINOR issue #529 tracks the duplicate failure notification shown after Retry.

title: stretch_clip fails on a just-reversed clip — it reads the proxy's length, not the source's
acceptance: stretch_clip on a clip whose reverse proxy has not rendered yet either succeeds (deriving from the SOURCE file length) or fails with an error that names the pending proxy. A --run-script of create -> stretch -> set_clip_reverse -> stretch succeeds on BOTH stretch calls.
notes: FOUND 2026-07-26 while gating PR #440. cmdStretchClip guards on ac->getAudioFile().getLength() <= 0.0 and returns 'source has no length'. set_clip_reverse installs an ASYNC proxy render; headless never pumps it, so the reversed clip's length stays 0 and stretch_clip refuses. Reproduced exactly with --run-script: stretch(ok) -> set_clip_reverse(ok) -> stretch('source has no length'). In the GUI the proxy usually renders fast enough to mask this, so the user-visible impact is a narrow race (reverse then immediately drag-to-stretch) rather than a hard break -- which is why it was filed, not fixed, inside a merge campaign. #440's persist matrix was reordered (stretch before reverse) to keep that fixture deterministic; the reorder is a TEST fix and does NOT address this. Same family as the documented 'reversed/warped proxies need __wait headless' gotcha.
